title: Design: client-side WhatsApp (DMA Art. 7) interop alongside MIMI, end-to-end encrypted
description:
Question from Mark (2026-11-13): Meta's DMA Article 7 offer says 'speak Signal to us'. Can mimid offer the MIMI-verse a way to reach WhatsApp users without breaking end-to-end encryption?

Ruled out: a server-side Signal-to-MLS bridge. It decrypts in the middle, breaks E2EE, almost certainly breaches Meta's partner terms (E2EE to the device; Meta can suspend partners), conflicts with Art. 7's requirement to preserve the security level, and has the Beeper Mini precedent with iMessage. Not to be built.

The idea: do it on the client, in the component that holds the MLS keys (mimid-agent, per the AGENTS.md crate map). The client speaks Signal and Meta's protocol to WhatsApp users and MLS to MIMI rooms, so no plaintext leaves the device. Offer it as a library or SDK for MIMI clients, not a hosted service.

Constraints from the 2026-11-13 research (IETF workspace research_notes/DMA messaging interop and MIMI/meta_reference_offer.md and commission_enforcement.md):
- Clients connect to Meta's servers with WhatsApp's own XMPP-based protocol, Noise transport and Meta-assigned identities; media goes through a Meta or third-party proxy.
- Encryption must be the Signal Protocol (Signal's code, or a Meta sub-licence) or something Meta confirms as 'equivalent'; no non-Signal approval is public. Not MLS.
- Native Android or iOS clients only; no multi-device; both users in the EEA (rechecked every 60 days); detailed documentation only under NDA; broad Meta suspension, termination and audit rights; 3 months to adopt documentation changes.
- The reference offer is per provider, so each MIMI provider shipping the SDK would sign its own contract with Meta. Whether one operator could sign as an aggregator for many MIMI providers is unknown; read the offer.
- Live today: only BirdyChat (now possibly Balsio) and Haiket, one-to-one only. Meta's offer covers groups since Sep 2025, but no partner ships interoperable groups. Calls are due 7 Sep 2027.
- Threema declined (2026-07-22): 'WhatsApp defines the protocols', so partners embed 'a light version' of Meta's app. Signal declined. Element built a 1:1 prototype (2024) but hasn't launched.

Open design questions:
1. Mixed rooms: a MIMI room with WhatsApp members can't be one MLS group. Each client would send every message twice, into the MLS group and pairwise Signal to the WhatsApp members, and room policy, membership and franking would have to account for that. Feasible, but at what group size? Or keep WhatsApp chats out of MIMI rooms entirely (1:1 bridged contacts only)?
2. Identity: Meta-assigned identities versus MIMI user URIs; how a mimid user appears to WhatsApp, and how discovery works (manual today, per BEREC).
3. Trust: keys for third-party users go through Meta. What key transparency is available to a partner (WhatsApp's Auditable Key Directory)?
4. Legal and operational: the Meta contract, GDPR role, security review, EEA-only users.
5. Licensing: Signal's libsignal is AGPL-3.0, which constrains how an SDK built on it can be shipped.

Next step: read Meta's current WhatsApp and Messenger reference offers (developers.facebook.com and the DMA portal) for the aggregator question and the documentation requirements, then write a short design note in this bead's design field for Mark's approval. Nothing is built until he approves.
